description: Composition of interviewers assigned to a specific interview, including their role on the panel (lead, technical, behavioral, debrief moderator) and weighting on the consolidated scorecard.
Question bank entry tied to competencies. Carries question text, type (behavioral / technical / situational), competency tags, suggested follow-ups, rubric.
Structured interviewer feedback against a defined rubric: per-competency ratings, written notes, and a hire/no-hire recommendation.
Bookable time window an interviewer has marked available. Drives self-serve scheduling (Goodtime / Modern Hire / Calendly for Recruiting). Carries interviewer, start, end, allowed interview types.
Scheduled assessment event between a candidate and one or more interviewers. Carries time, location/medium, panel, interview kit, and outcome.
A recertification record: an owner attests that a piece of content is current, or flags it stale for remediation or archival.
Derived freshness, quality, accessibility, and ownership-coverage score per inventory record.
A discovered or registered piece of intranet content (page, hub, space, library, form) across connected intranets, with source, type, last-modified, owner, and governance status.
Assignment of an accountable owner and backup to an inventory record, with the review cadence the owner is responsible for.
A governed content-type definition (policy, news post, hub, library, form, FAQ) carrying its default review cadence, criticality, and retention rule.

Scheduled or ad-hoc inventory count session: location, item-filter scope (ABC class, last-counted-before, all), assigned counter, status (scheduled, counting, variance_review, posted), per-line variances.
INV-MGMT-scoped lot or batch identifier: lot_code, item, supplier, manufacture_date, expiry_date, originating receipt. Distinct from FDS `traceability_lots` (FSMA-204 food-traceability scope).
Bill-of-kit for sellable bundles: parent item, list of component items with quantities, assembly_required flag (vs. explode-at-order).
Item by location replenishment policy: reorder_point, reorder_quantity, safety_stock, lead_time_days, preferred_supplier, auto_generate_po flag.
Individually-tracked unit with a unique serial: item, current location, current status (in_stock, reserved, issued, returned, scrapped), warranty_start.
Per-item by per-location quantity record: on_hand, reserved, in_transit, available_for_allocation. Real-time maintained by stock_movements; not directly edited.

Inventory-scoped item record: SKU, unit of measure, lot/serial-controlled flag, ABC/XYZ class, default cost method (FIFO, LIFO, weighted-average), weight, and dimensions. INV-MGMT-mastered for standalone deployments; embedded-masters `commerce_products` when B2C-COMM is canonical.
INV-MGMT's finer-grain location catalog: warehouse, store, bin, zone, or hub. Defers to OMS `inventory_locations` (canonical) when present; deployable standalone otherwise.
Append-only event ledger of inventory transactions: receipt, issue, transfer-in, transfer-out, adjustment-positive, adjustment-negative. Underlies stock_balances; posted movements are immutable.

Inter-location transfer header with lines: source location, destination location, requested-by user, status (requested, approved, in_transit, received, discrepancy, reconciled), expected arrival date.
Stock-location catalog: location_code, type (warehouse / store / 3pl / hub), on_hand, reserved, available_for_allocation. WMS will co-master balances when loaded.
A preserved evidence artifact attached to an insider-risk case (file copy, activity snapshot, screen capture, lineage trace, exported report) with chain-of-custody metadata for HR and Legal review.
Fund entity (name, vintage, size, type, GP, fee schedule, dissolution date) — organizes capital calls + distributions.
Internal IC document per deal capturing thesis, financials, risks, deal-team commentary, and IC vote. Locked at final IC vote.

Real-estate asset held for investment return (acquired/operated/disposed for cash flow and appreciation); carries acquisition basis, debt structure, current valuation, NOI history. Distinct from REAL-EST `real_estate_properties` (the corporate-tenant occupancy view) — same physical asset can underlie both rows in different domains.

People in the firm's external network: founders, executives, co-investors, advisors, LP-side contacts. Distinct from CRM's customer-side `contacts`. The minimum-embedded-shape is the GDPR-relevant subset every module embedding this record must support.

Three-way-match outcome record: invoice, purchase_order, goods_receipt with line-level match status (matched / quantity_variance / price_variance / no_po / exception). Drives auto-post or exception-queue routing.
A candidate's submission against a specific requisition. Carries pipeline stage, status (active / rejected / withdrawn / hired), source, and the full evaluation history.
Formal employment offer extended to a candidate. Carries compensation components, start date, terms, approval chain, and status (draft / approved / sent / accepted / declined / rescinded).
Syndication of a job_posting to an external board (LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor, internal mobility portal). Carries board name, post timestamp, expiry, cost, applicant attribution.
Published, candidate-facing version of a requisition on a career site or job board. One requisition can have many postings (per board, language, or region).

Canonical role definition in the job catalog: title, family, level, responsibilities, required skills and competencies, pay range, FLSA classification. Distinct from positions (which are slots referencing a profile). Many positions share a single job profile.
Approved request to hire for a specific role. The master ATS work item, carries headcount, level, location, hiring manager, recruiter, and status (draft / open / on_hold / filled / canceled).
Individual posting to the general ledger: header (date, source, period) plus balanced debit / credit lines tagged with GL account, cost center, dimension members. The atomic accounting unit.
Sequential node in an experience flow (step 1 → step 2 → exit).
FSMA-204-defined KDE attached to a CTE; sortable into FDA spreadsheet response format.
Knowledge-graph-platform-mastered entities — distinct from DATA-AI-PLAT shared knowledge_graph_entities.
Knowledge-graph-platform-specific ontology. Distinct from DATA-AI-PLAT shared ontologies.
KB content backing both self-service portals and agent-assist tooling. Lifecycle: draft → review → published → retired. Quality and freshness are the silent ITSM KPIs that drive deflection rate.

Authored, versioned content unit. The KMS standalone-market master, distinct from ITSM/CSM/HRSD/LSD bundled `knowledge_articles` (which are platform-embedded). Lifecycle: draft → published → archived.
Hierarchical organization of articles (topics, sections, tags, search facets).
Curated groupings of articles (product docs, process guides, FAQs, onboarding playbooks). Audience tags + expiration.

Typed instances of ontology classes — RDF named individuals or LPG nodes — with assertions, relationships, embeddings, and provenance. The 'data' tier of a knowledge graph that AI agents query and operational apps write back to.
Logged search events for analytics; identifies gaps (zero-result queries).
Cluster resource: name, version, control-plane config, network CIDR, CNI choice, feature gates, API-server settings.

External labor-market overlay used to validate plan assumptions: availability, prevailing salary, time-to-hire, and supply concentration by role × geography × level. Typically sourced from third-party labor-market data providers rather than generated internally; the SWP-side record is the imported/cached view used for planning.
Per-cow per-lactation cycle: calving date, dry-off date, peak milk yield, 305-day projection, days-in-milk.

Registered table or view in the platform catalog, materialized over open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi) on object storage or as native warehouse tables. Carries catalog/schema/name, ownership, tags, classification, format metadata, and a pointer to the underlying physical layout. The unit of data on which lineage, governance, BI queries, and ML training all sit.
A cross-functional task within a launch plan, assigned to a function and tied to a milestone.
A dated checkpoint inside a launch plan (kickoff, content-complete, sales-ready, GA).
A working go-to-market plan for a launch: scope, milestones, readiness gate, and owners.
User-built application on the low-code platform: name, owner, deployment, permissions, status. The unit of LCAP delivery.
Custom domain object defined within an LCAP app: schema, fields, references, validation rules, security model. The data layer of the LCAP delivery.
Configured external connection (CRM, database, REST API) bound to a low-code app with schema introspection.
UI screen or page authored as a versioned LCAP application artifact (page, screen, or canvas).
Business process definition inside an LCAP app: states, transitions, role-based steps, integrations, escalations. The behavior layer of the LCAP delivery.

Scoring records per lead/contact — explicit signals (form-fill, demo-request, content-download) + implicit signals (behavior, fit/firmographic match). The mechanism behind the MQL handoff to CRM; thresholds and decay rules drive routing.
Earned-badge junction per learner per badge; carries earn date, evidence URL, and verification token.
Issued credential against a worker (internal certification, vendor cert, regulatory cert) with issue date, expiry, issuing body, and renewal rules. Drives recertification campaigns.
Per-learner sent-notification log row for reminders, nudges, completions, and escalations.
Reusable content asset (video, PDF, image, audio) referenced by lessons and modules.
Path-to-learner assignment row distinct from course_enrollments; tracks overall path progress and completion percentage.
Ordered step inside a learning path: pointer to a course, sub-path, or external resource with sequencing rules.
Curated sequence of courses targeting a role, skill, or certification. Drives ordered enrollment and progress tracking across multiple courses.
Personalized plan composed of multiple paths or courses, often manager-curated or AI-recommended against skill gaps.
Per-learner suggested content generated from skill gaps and role profile.
Granular completion event for a course or activity, often xAPI / SCORM / cmi5 statement: actor, verb, object, result, timestamp. Feeds skill_profiles and certifications.

The lessee lease contract as the accounting subledger record: parties, leased asset, commencement and end dates, term, options, components, and the payment terms the accounting is built from. The lessee-accounting view, distinct from the workplace occupancy record and the landlord operations record.

The classification decision for a lease and its supporting test results: finance versus operating for ASC 842 lessees (and lessor sales-type, direct-financing, operating buckets); single lessee model under IFRS 16. Re-tested on modification.
A tracked obligation deadline on a lease: option-exercise windows, renewal and notice dates, rent reviews, and termination deadlines, with alerting so the obligation is acted on before it lapses.

A prepared lease-accounting disclosure for a reporting period: weighted-average discount rate and remaining term, maturity analysis of undiscounted cash flows, lease cost by type, and the standard reconciliations, frozen once filed.
A source document attached to a lease: the executed contract, amendments, abstracts, and correspondence that evidence the terms feeding the accounting.
The lease liability measured at the present value of unpaid lease payments, unwound with effective interest over the lease term and remeasured on modification or reassessment.

A change to a lease and its accounting consequence: scope or consideration changes, remeasurements, reassessments, discount-rate updates, index and rate true-ups, and right-of-use asset impairment, with before-and-after balances.
The period-by-period schedule of lease cash flows, liability amortization (principal and interest), and right-of-use asset amortization that drives recognition and the maturity-analysis disclosure.
Documented legal opinion / consultation: matter or requestor reference, advice narrative, applicability scope, confidence, expiry/review date, privilege classification.

Court-centric tracking for litigated matters: court/jurisdiction, case number, judge, calendar (filing, hearing, trial, appeal dates), opposing counsel, key documents. Subset of in_house_legal_matters with litigation metadata.

Canonical contract record: counterparty / supplier, contract type (MSA, SOW, NDA, DPA, subscription, lease), effective and expiry dates, total value, governing law, status (draft, in-negotiation, signed, active, expired, terminated). The most multi-mastered SaaS-related object — CLM owns the document, S2P and SMP contribute context.
Statutory company: legal name, registration, jurisdiction, currency, fiscal calendar. Books are kept per legal entity; consolidation rolls them up.

eDiscovery / litigation preservation notice: matter reference, affected record types (email, documents, messages, files), custodian scope, issued date, lifting date. Drives enforcement across data systems.

Demand-signal record: business-unit request for legal advice or service. Carries description, priority, required-by date, requesting department, triage outcome (matter creation / policy guidance / escalation). The front door to LSD.

Law-firm matter (case, transaction, advisory engagement): client, opposing parties, matter type, key dates (statute of limitations, court dates), responsible attorneys, billing rates, status. The central organizing entity of law-firm operations.
Leaf consumable inside a course module: video, document, SCORM block, or live activity.
Order for library materials from a book vendor, including line items, fund allocations, EDI exchange status, and receiving workflow.
Controlled-vocabulary record for a name, subject, organization, or uniform title used as a heading in bibliographic records, supporting consistent retrieval and disambiguation.
Configuration rule defining loan period, renewal limits, fine accrual, and hold behavior for a combination of item type and patron category.
License agreement for an electronic resource (database, ebook collection, ejournal package), including authorized users, concurrent-user limits, ILL permissions, and renewal terms.
Monetary charge against a patron account for overdue, lost, or damaged library items, including assessment, payment, and waiver workflow.
Summary of which copies of a bibliographic record exist at a given location, including coverage statements for serials and shelf-location information.
Patron request to reserve a bibliographic record or specific item for later pickup, including position in queue, pickup location, and trap status.
Physical or digital copy of a work held by the library. One bibliographic record may have many items, each with its own barcode, location, status, and circulation history.
Circulation transaction recording the loan of a library item to a patron, including due date, renewal history, and return status.
Classification of patrons (e.g. student, faculty, staff, public, juvenile) that drives circulation policy and access entitlement.

Registered library member with borrowing privileges, contact information, patron category, and account history. Distinct from platform users; a patron may or may not have a linked user account for self-service.
Patron-owned saved query or reading list in the discovery layer, optionally configured to send alerts when new matching items are added to the catalog.
Active subscription to a periodical or other continuing resource, including issue prediction, check-in records, claim history, and renewal schedule.
Partner library or consortium member with which this library participates in resource sharing, including agreement terms, default lending policies, and contact endpoints.
Book or serials vendor relationship managed by the library, including account credentials, EDI settings, claiming defaults, and contact information.
